title: Federal Register: Express Scripts, Inc., et al.; Analysis of Agreement Containing Consent Order To Aid Public Comment (FTC Docket No. 9437)

history.reason: Source downloaded from GovInfo and read on the access date; findings transcribed from the extracted text.

publisher: Federal Trade Commission (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government notice of proposed consent order with FTC analysis
reliability: Government document. The issuing agency is a party with its own policy interest (CMS: rulemaking; FTC: enforcement and study). The FTC is the enforcer proposing the settlement; the notice describes allegations and terms, not adjudicated findings.
findings: The FTC states the proposed consent agreement settles (1) the Insulin Litigation alleging Section 5 violations over rebate-driven competition and (2) a separate PBM Investigation into whether Express Scripts (ESI) unlawfully harmed pharmacy or PBM competition; comments were due March 16, 2026.

The FTC states the PBM Investigation sought to determine whether ESI violated Section 5 by requiring clients' members to use its affiliated pharmacies or by coercing unaffiliated pharmacies to accept unfavorable contractual terms.

Section VIII of the proposed order requires ESI to develop a standard offering for retail community pharmacies (defined as a pharmacy business with three or fewer retail stores) that compensates based on actual drug acquisition cost plus a dispensing fee, pays for non-dispensing services, and does not exclude willing community pharmacies.

Under Section IX ESI must advertise its standard offerings, and the notice states the order is a proposed, accepted-subject-to-final-approval consent agreement placed on the public record for 30 days.
limitations: A proposed consent order; the notice describes allegations, not findings of liability, and the scope of the PBM Investigation allegations is stated in general terms.
Applies to ESI only (and, per the notice, with Cigna-related terms); other PBMs are covered by separate matters not read here.
Final approval, final text and any later compliance outcome were not read or verified. CMS (source above) states a Caremark settlement followed in July 2026; that order was not read.
No data on how many independent pharmacies would use the standard offering or whether it changes net payments.
